spec_match.rationale: Drives the two exact surfaces whose contracts the feature changes — navigator.setAppBadge()/clearAppBadge() (now permission-gated on macOS) and the requireInteraction notification option (now ignored for app notifications) — and states both new contracts precisely, including that setAppBadge still resolves while the OS silently shows nothing.

interactive.rationale: Three real badging calls (numeric, flag-only, clear) with verbatim promise outcomes, a requireInteraction checkbox + show button that reads the value back off the live Notification object, and a permission-request button; every branch reports into live status lines.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index promises driving the real setAppBadge/clearAppBadge and requireInteraction surfaces; the page does exactly that.

edge_cases.rationale: Handles Badging-API-missing, promise rejection, not-installed context (no icon to badge — stated as the environment's honest limit), permission-not-granted for notifications, requireInteraction-member-missing, and platform-dependent persistence explanations.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5863296436666368 and the spec's requireInteraction anchor.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite asserts the badging methods and requireInteraction member this page exercises; verified passing on this browser, with the OS-side behavior change correctly living in the manual assertion.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 verified via ?autorun: setAppBadge(3) genuinely resolved, context line reports browser-tab-on-Linux honestly, requireInteraction path reports the permission-default cannot-show fallback, console clean, 0 overflow at true 360; the granted-permission notification and a real visible badge require an installed app and a manual run.

telemetry_health.rationale: badge-call-resolved/rejected and ri-roundtrip assert the real outcomes; badge-fallback-honest, ri-fallback-honest, and ri-permission-fallback-honest report every fallback branch separately.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only, checkbox uses accent-color, contract matrix in .table-scroll, statuses on bg-stone with black text (AA), no button colour overrides.

accessibility.rationale: The requireInteraction toggle is a real labelled checkbox with 44px hit area, all outcomes land in aria-live polite outputs, table headers use scope=col.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at 1280x1800 and true 360 (iframe harness): 0px overflow, buttons stack full-width, the three-column contract matrix scrolls inside its container instead of widening the page.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Boolean options should be native checkboxes with a bound visible label and adequate target size.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: requireInteraction is a native checkbox inside a flex label with min-height 44px and accent-color from the design system.

guidanceConsulted.query: async action result announcement live region
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Async API outcomes must be announced via text in live regions, distinguishing success, rejection, and unsupported.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Badge and notification outcomes write distinct verbatim messages (resolved / rejected+name / API missing / permission blocked) into aria-live outputs.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel narrow mobile no horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Wide tables belong in their own overflow-x container; grid children need min-width:0.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The contract matrix sits in .table-scroll and .lab children carry min-width:0; measured 0 page overflow at true 360.

openQuestions.title: Observe the real badge no-op and requireInteraction-ignore on macOS
openQuestions.detail: Only an installed PWA on macOS Chrome 130+ with the flag can show the contract changes: badge invisible until notifications permission is granted, and a requireInteraction:true banner auto-dismissing under the Banners alert style. Record both observations and fold them into the page copy as verified evidence.

openQuestions.title: Badge value readback is impossible — consider stating it explicitly
openQuestions.detail: The Badging API has no getter, so the page can only report promise resolution; a sentence noting the API is intentionally write-only would preempt the obvious question of why no badge state is displayed.

summary: Genuine Badging API and requireInteraction exercises wired to honest per-environment context (browser-tab-on-Linux: promise resolves, nothing can be visible, and the page says so). Autorun-verified on headless Chromium 141 desktop + true-360 mobile with clean console and zero overflow; the macOS-visible halves of both contract changes are recorded as manual follow-ups.
